name: AI FieldGuide Academy
tagline: Learn AI. Apply it. Make it work.
promise: A guided, practical path from AI-curious to AI-capable at work and in the real world.
disclaimer: Training improves skills but does not guarantee employment, income, business results, or error-free AI output.

modules.title: AI Foundations Without the Hype
modules.outcome: Explain what modern AI can and cannot do, then choose a safe first use case.
modules.project: Build your personal AI opportunity-and-risk map.
lessons: AI, language models, and generative AI in plain English
Prediction versus understanding: why confident errors happen
The human review loop for important work
Privacy, permissions, copyright, bias, and workplace policy

modules.title: ChatGPT for Everyday Work
modules.outcome: Turn vague tasks into useful drafts, analyses, plans, and reusable workflows.
modules.project: Create a five-task ChatGPT workbench for your role.
lessons: Choosing the right task and supplying trustworthy context
Drafting, summarizing, analyzing, and brainstorming
Working with documents and structured information
Verification, privacy, and when not to use AI

modules.title: Claude and Claude Cowork
modules.outcome: Delegate a bounded knowledge-work outcome while keeping consequential decisions human-controlled.
modules.project: Turn a folder of source material into a reviewed deliverable.
lessons: Claude for writing, research, analysis, and long-form context
Claude Cowork: goal-based work across approved files and apps
Folder boundaries, connector permissions, and review checkpoints
Building a repeatable knowledge-work playbook

modules.title: Claude Code: Build by Describing Outcomes
modules.outcome: Use an agentic coding workflow to inspect, change, test, and review a small project.
modules.project: Build and test a useful one-page tool.
lessons: Terminal basics and a safe project workspace
Context files, task briefs, and acceptance criteria
Plan, edit, test, inspect: the agentic coding loop
Permissions, secrets, version control, and rollback

modules.title: AI Agents in the Real World
modules.outcome: Design an agent workflow with clear tools, boundaries, evidence, and stop conditions.
modules.project: Map a safe research-to-draft agent for your work.
lessons: What makes an agent different from a chat
Goals, context, tools, memory, actions, and evaluation
Human approval gates and blast-radius limits
Monitoring cost, quality, failures, and drift

modules.title: PROMPT LIKE A P.R.O.
modules.outcome: Write prompts that produce clearer, more verifiable work across leading AI tools.
modules.project: Create three P.R.O. prompts for a real weekly task.
lessons: P — Purpose: outcome, audience, and definition of done
R — Relevant context: sources, constraints, examples, and assumptions
O — Output contract: format, tone, length, checks, and next step
Prompt debugging: isolate one weak variable at a time

modules.title: The 20 Must-Know Prompts
modules.outcome: Adapt twenty reusable prompt patterns instead of starting from a blank box.
modules.project: Save a role-specific prompt library with examples and quality checks.
lessons: Communication and meeting prompts
Research, decisions, and analysis prompts
Planning, systems, and agent prompts
Career, customer, and offer-building prompts

modules.title: The Useful AI Tools Map
modules.outcome: Select tools by job, evidence, risk, and total cost—not hype.
modules.project: Build a three-tool stack and a quarterly review checklist.
lessons: General assistants, research tools, and document tools
Coding agents, automation, image, audio, and video tools
Connectors, data access, and vendor lock-in
The tool scorecard: fit, quality, privacy, price, and exit plan

modules.title: Build Income With AI—Responsibly
modules.outcome: Package one real customer problem into a small, testable AI-assisted offer.
modules.project: Create and validate a one-page service or digital-product offer.
lessons: Skills first: solve a painful problem before choosing tools
Service, productized service, templates, training, and software
Customer interviews, honest claims, pricing, and a paid pilot
Simple funnel metrics: visitors, leads, buyers, retention, and MRR

modules.title: 30-Day AI WorkReady Capstone
modules.outcome: Deliver a verified portfolio artifact and a repeatable AI workflow.
modules.project: Complete a before-and-after workflow case study with evidence.
lessons: Week 1: baseline the task, time, quality, and risk
Week 2: prototype prompts and compare outputs
Week 3: add automation, approvals, and evaluation
Week 4: document results, limitations, and next iteration

reasons.title: AI literacy is becoming basic work literacy
reasons.copy: Learn the vocabulary, limits, and decision habits needed to participate confidently in AI-enabled workplaces.

reasons.title: Stop losing hours to repeatable work
reasons.copy: Find tasks AI can accelerate while keeping judgment and accountability with you.

reasons.title: Better prompts create better starting points
reasons.copy: Use the P.R.O. framework to replace vague requests with clear outcomes, context, and output standards.

reasons.title: Choose tools without chasing every trend
reasons.copy: Evaluate assistants, agents, and creative tools by fit, privacy, evidence, cost, and exit options.

reasons.title: Turn scattered experiments into workflows
reasons.copy: Build reusable processes with inputs, checkpoints, quality tests, and definitions of done.

reasons.title: Agents require boundaries, not blind trust
reasons.copy: Learn permissions, approval gates, monitoring, and stop conditions before an agent acts.

reasons.title: Protect private and high-stakes information
reasons.copy: Recognize sensitive data, follow workplace policy, and avoid placing confidential material in the wrong tool.

reasons.title: Show employers what you can actually do
reasons.copy: Finish with a portfolio-ready case study that documents the task, workflow, evidence, and limitations.

reasons.title: Test income ideas without fake promises
reasons.copy: Package a useful skill into a paid pilot and measure demand before spending heavily.

reasons.title: Willie keeps help close
reasons.copy: Your AI Wisdom Guide is available across the academy to explain lessons, adapt examples, and help you find the next step.

prompts.name: The Outcome Brief
prompts.template: Purpose: Help me produce [outcome] for [audience] by [date]. Relevant context: [facts, source material, constraints, examples]. Output contract: Return [format] with [required sections]. Identify assumptions and end with the three most important next actions.

prompts.name: The Executive Summary
prompts.template: Summarize the material below for [audience]. Preserve decisions, numbers, risks, owners, and deadlines. Separate confirmed facts from assumptions. Output: a five-bullet brief followed by a 100-word explanation. Material: [paste or attach].

prompts.name: The Decision Memo
prompts.template: I must decide [decision]. Context: [context]. Compare [options] against [criteria]. State what evidence is missing, list reversible versus irreversible consequences, and recommend a next step without pretending uncertainty is resolved.

prompts.name: The Meeting Prep
prompts.template: Prepare me for a meeting with [people] about [topic]. Based only on [sources], give me the likely goals, five questions, three risks, my desired outcome, and a concise opening statement. Flag anything that must be verified.

prompts.name: Notes to Action
prompts.template: Turn these notes into an action record. Output: decisions, open questions, action items with owner and due date, risks, and a follow-up email. Do not invent missing owners or deadlines; label them TBD. Notes: [notes].

prompts.name: The Clear Email
prompts.template: Rewrite this email for [recipient] so the purpose and requested action are clear. Keep my facts and intent. Tone: [tone]. Maximum [length]. Add a specific subject line and flag any wording that could be misunderstood. Draft: [text].

prompts.name: The Research Plan
prompts.template: Create a research plan for [question]. Define scope, key terms, primary sources, recency requirements, disconfirming evidence, and a stop condition. Do not answer the question yet. Output a numbered plan and an evidence table template.

prompts.name: The Claim Checker
prompts.template: Audit the claims below. For each, label it supported, uncertain, outdated, opinion, or contradicted. Explain what source would verify it. Quote no more than necessary and do not create citations. Claims: [claims].

prompts.name: The Customer Lens
prompts.template: Analyze this offer for [specific customer]. Separate known evidence from hypotheses. List the top job-to-be-done, pains, desired outcomes, objections, and language to test in interviews. Do not fabricate customer quotes. Offer: [offer].

prompts.name: The Content Multiplier
prompts.template: Repurpose the source below into one email, three short posts, a 60-second video outline, and five FAQ answers. Preserve the source's meaning, remove unsupported claims, and adapt each format to [audience]. Source: [content].

prompts.name: The SOP Builder
prompts.template: Turn this process into a standard operating procedure for a new team member. Include purpose, inputs, permissions, steps, quality checks, exceptions, escalation points, and definition of done. Process notes: [notes].

prompts.name: The Data Questioner
prompts.template: Help me analyze [dataset or table]. First inspect definitions and data quality. Then answer [questions], show calculations, distinguish correlation from causation, and list limitations. Do not infer missing values without labeling the method.

prompts.name: Constrained Brainstorm
prompts.template: Generate 12 ideas for [goal] within these constraints: [budget, time, audience, rules]. Group them into safe, bold, and experimental. Score each for impact, effort, and uncertainty. Recommend two inexpensive tests.

prompts.name: Stakeholder Rehearsal
prompts.template: Role-play a skeptical [stakeholder] reviewing [proposal]. Ask one question at a time about value, evidence, risk, cost, and implementation. After my answers, summarize the strongest objection and how I can improve the proposal honestly.

prompts.name: Explain the Code
prompts.template: Explain this code to a [beginner/intermediate] learner. Describe its purpose, data flow, dependencies, risky operations, and one small example. Then list questions I should answer before changing it. Code: [code or file].

prompts.name: Debug With Evidence
prompts.template: Diagnose this failure. Evidence: [error, logs, steps, environment]. Rank likely causes, state what would confirm each, and give the smallest safe diagnostic step first. Do not propose destructive changes or claim a fix is verified until tests pass.

prompts.name: The Agent Task Contract
prompts.template: Design an agent task for [goal]. Specify allowed inputs, tools, actions, forbidden actions, budget, evidence requirements, approval gates, retry limit, stop conditions, and final output schema. Keep consequential decisions with a human.

prompts.name: The Project Plan
prompts.template: Plan [project] for [deadline]. Break it into milestones with owner, dependency, acceptance test, risk, and fallback. Identify the critical path and the first reversible action. Context: [context].

prompts.name: Prompt Repair
prompts.template: Improve the prompt below using P.R.O.: Purpose, Relevant context, Output contract. Preserve its goal, identify the three biggest ambiguities, then provide a revised prompt and a short test case. Original prompt: [prompt].

prompts.name: The Paid Pilot
prompts.template: Turn my skill [skill] and customer problem [problem] into a small paid pilot. Define the customer, bounded deliverable, exclusions, timeline, evidence of value, price hypothesis, outreach message, and success/failure criteria. Avoid income guarantees and unsupported claims.
